citeAs: The EgoLife Team (2025). EgoLife: Towards Egocentric Life Assistant. arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.03803v1.
creator: The EgoLife Team
description: A 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset with intensive annotation, collected from six participants living together for one week.
name: EgoLife
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The 100K QA candidates were filtered down to 1K high-quality questions per participant for further meticulous revision. This final round of curation resulted in a carefully crafted set of 500 QA per participant.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Capcut (video editing software with dubbing functions)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: AI-generated questions were provided to annotators as SRT files, acting as a filtering and inspiration tool. Annotators retained questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior, with a preference for longer dependencies and real-world relevance. Annotators also generated distractors for multiple-choice questions.
rai:dataCollection: Six participants shared a fully instrumented living environment, recording approximately eight hours of egocentric multimodal video daily using Meta Aria glasses. 15 additional cameras and two mmWave devices captured synchronized third-person perspectives.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Due to storage limitations, recordings are structured into three-hour segments. The glasses are collected every three hours for data upload and storage clearance. During this period, participants are instructed to remain in their rooms and limit their activities to resting or non-essential tasks to prevent logic disruptions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: First-person video from AI glasses, third-person video from fixed indoor cameras, and synchronized multimodal signal data including millimeter-wave radars and WiFi signals.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Seven-day period (Beijing session) and a one-day session (Milan session).
rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Direct measurement, Passive Data Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset intentionally started with a narrow setting to build a strong foundation, sacrificing some generalizability (e.g., single language/scenario).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All faces and sensitive visual data were blurred. Any sensitive topics in audio were muted to protect participant privacy.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The pipeline synchronizes multi-source data (video, audio, IMU) from Aria glasses and GoPro cameras using the EgoSync codebase, processes them through privacy protection (EgoBlur), dense captioning (EgoCaption), and transcription (EgoTranscript) modules.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand the dataset to cover a broader range of languages, locations, and activities.
rai:dataSocialImpact: EgoButler’s advancements may ultimately foster a new era of AI companions capable of supporting individuals in a socially and ethically responsible manner. By promoting real-time, context-aware AI, this work aims to benefit society, encouraging safe, meaningful, and privacy-conscious interactions between humans and AI.
rai:dataUseCases: Long-context, life-oriented question-answering tasks that assess the effectiveness of personalized AI assistance, addressing practical needs such as locating misplaced items, recalling past events, tracking health habits, analyzing social interactions, and making timely recommendations.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Whisper Large v3 (speech recognition), and an open-source diarization algorithm.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Participant faces, bystanders' faces, vehicle license plates, sensitive audio segments containing private or potentially identifiable information, and sensitive screen content (e.g., mobile or computer screens displaying passwords or personal data).
